overview: The Homes for Heroes Act changes the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) home loan program, in which the VA guarantees part of a mortgage so veterans can borrow with better terms. For certain veterans, it raises the maximum amount of the VA's guarantee from 25 percent to 37.5 percent of the national conforming loan limit, the size cap for mortgages backed by the company Freddie Mac. It also changes the fee the VA charges on "interest rate reduction refinancing loans," which let veterans refinance an existing VA loan to a lower rate: the fee would drop to 0.25 percent of the loan from the end of 2025 through 2027, then rise in stages to as high as 0.75 percent from October 2031 through 2035 before settling at 0.50 percent. As of September 18, 2025, the House Veterans' Affairs Committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say a larger VA guarantee would help veterans who have already used part of their home loan benefit buy homes in higher-cost markets, and lower refinancing fees in the near term would help veterans cut their monthly payments.
against: Critics say expanding the guarantee increases the government's exposure if borrowers default, and raising refinancing fees in later years means some future veterans would pay more to help cover the cost.
